findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so database storage, snapshots and backups are written unencrypted with no KMS customer-managed key.
publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public IP address, exposing the database endpoint to the internet rather than keeping it in a private subnet layer.
The master username is the default 'admin', a predictable account name that facilitates credential-guessing attacks against the publicly reachable instance.

The master password is supplied from var.password in plain Terraform variable form and stored in state/plan output rather than being generated or retrieved from Secrets Manager, risking credential leakage.

The user_data script interpolates the database endpoint, username and plaintext password into an EC2 launch script; user data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstances/instance metadata access and is stored unencrypted.
No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled; an SSRF in the PHP application would allow unauthenticated retrieval of the instance role's credentials, which are highly privileged here.
No root_block_device encryption is specified, so the instance's volumes (which hold the dbinfo.inc file containing the DB password) may be created unencrypted.
The instance is placed in a public subnet and its public DNS is exported, serving an HTTP-only PHP application with no TLS, so application traffic including form submissions travels unencrypted.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", far exceeding least privilege; combined with IMDSv1 this effectively hands an attacker near-administrative control of storage, compute and databases.
The database security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing a data exfiltration and command-and-control path.
The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the application-to-database connection can be established unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: database security group with public exposure
findings.description: This security group is attached to a publicly accessible RDS instance; the combination of public accessibility and only VPC-CIDR ingress relies solely on the SG, and no explicit restriction of default/egress behaviour is defined on the group itself.
